qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary fashion luxury and leather goods heavily dependent on trend cycles (Gucci), easily forgone and deferred in downturns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Discretionary fashion apparel and trend-driven leather goods (Gucci over-reliance) are non-essential and easily forgone during economic downturns. The brand lacks the multi-generational Lindy pricing power of Hermès or Cartier, suffering severe volume contraction when fashion trends shift.
qualitative.evidence: Kering SA has suffered severe earnings contraction due to Gucci's brand fatigue and fashion cycle unwinding. Recurring operating income plunged from €4.75B in 2023 to €2.44B in 2024 and €1.63B in 2025. ROIC fell from ~16% (2022) to ~11% (2023) and ~3.4-5% in 2024-2025. Unlike secular luxury compounders, Kering carried €8.0B to €10.5B in net debt following debt-funded acquisitions (Creed for ~€3.5B, 30% of Valentino, and prime real estate purchases at cycle peaks), leading S&P to downgrade its credit rating to BBB+. The business model is highly cyclical, discretionary, and fashion-trend sensitive.
